content: Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of progesterone by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs or nonhormonal contraceptives are recommended. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of quizartinib, ranolazine, repotrectinib, rimegepant, ripretinib, selpercatinib, selumetinib, silodosin, simvastatin, siponimod, sirolimus, sofosbuvir, sofosbuvir/velpatasvir, sonidegib, sorafenib, sotorasib, stiripentol, tazemetostat, tezacaftor, tipranavir, tivozanib, tolvaptan, tovorafenib, trabectedin, trazodone, trimipramine, tucatinib, typhoid vaccine live, ubrogepant, ulipristal, upadacitinib, valbenazine, velpatasvir, vemurafenib, venetoclax, voclosporin, vonoprazan, vorapaxar, voxilaprevir, zuranolone, and abiraterone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Rifapentine decreases ritonavir levels by increasing its metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. Rifapentine reduces the efficacy of rolapitant when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Avoid coadministration if possible. Rifapentine decreases the levels of almontriptan, alprazolam, amiodarone, amitriptyline, amlodipine, aprepitant, aripiprazole, atorvastatin, avanafil, avatrombopag, bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens, belumosudil, benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen, bexarotene, bortezomib, brentuximab vedotin, brexpiprazole, bromocriptine, budesonide, buprenorphine (including buccal and long-acting injection forms), buspirone, cabazitaxel, calcifediol, cannabidiol, carbamazepine, carvedilol, cilostazol, cinacalcet, citalopram, clomipramine, and clonazepam by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. For specific drugs like abiraterone, atogepant, belumosudil, brexpiprazole, and benzhydrocodone, dosage adjustments or therapy modifications are recommended when coadministered with rifapentine. Rifapentine decreases the levels of typhoid vaccine live through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Coadministration is contraindicated. Rifapentine reduces the levels of calcifediol by stimulating microsomal hydroxylation, thereby shortening its half-life. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Rifapentine decreases the levels of cannabidiol. Consider increasing the cannabidiol dosage based on clinical response and tolerability. Rifapentine decreases carvedilol levels by increasing its metabolism via CYP2C9/10. Use caution and monitor closely. Rifapentine decreases the levels of tavorafenib, a CYP2C8 substrate. Avoid coadministration with strong or moderate CYP2C8 inducers. For drugs like buprenorphine long-acting injection, ensure adequate plasma levels are maintained. If levels are insufficient and CYP3A4 inducers cannot be reduced, transition back to a formulation that allows dose adjustments.
